1.note: Here, **And it will be** marks a transition to a new section about blessings. If the connection between this statement and the previous one is not clear, you may want to use a different connecting word to show how this section relates to what comes before it. Alternate translation: [Now] or [Next]

Moses is repeating forms of the verb **listen** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [you listen carefully] or [you really listen]

Here the word **listen** means to intentionally hear and obey. You could say that explicitly if that would be helpful to your readers. See the discussion about this in the Introduction to Deuteronomy for further information. Alternate translation: [you are obedient]

Here, **voice** represents the words that Yahweh spoke, which include his commands. See the discussion about this in the introduction to this chapter for further information. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [to what Yahweh you God says]
See how you translated the phrase “Yahweh your God” in 1:10.

1.q: וּ⁠נְתָ֨נְ⁠ךָ֜ יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֨י⁠ךָ֙ עֶלְי֔וֹן עַ֖ל כָּל־גּוֹיֵ֥י
1.note: Here Moses is speaking of making Israel prominent and powerful among other nations as if he would physically **set you high above all the nations**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. See how you translated the same expression in 26:19. Alternate translation: [then Yahweh your God will make you more prominent than all the other nations] or [then Yahweh your God will make you more powerful than all the other nations]

2.note: Here Moses is speaking of **blessings** as if they were living beings that could **come upon** and **reach** a person by chasing and capturing them. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Yahweh will give you all these blessings]

2.q: וּ⁠בָ֧אוּ עָלֶ֛י⁠ךָ כָּל־הַ⁠בְּרָכ֥וֹת הָ⁠אֵ֖לֶּה וְ⁠הִשִּׂיגֻ֑⁠ךָ כִּ֣י תִשְׁמַ֔ע בְּ⁠ק֖וֹל יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶֽי⁠ךָ
2.note: Moses is presenting a possible condition, that Yahweh will only bless the Israelites if they listen to and obey what Yahweh said. Use a natural form in your language for introducing a condition that could happen. It may be helpful to reorder this sentence so that the conditional statement is first. Alternate translation: [If you listen to the voice of Yahweh your God, then all these blessings will come on you and reach you]

Moses assumes that readers will know that **listen** as it is used here, includes the meaning of “obey.” You could say that explicitly if that would be helpful to your readers. See the discussion about this in the Introduction to Deuteronomy for further information. Alternate translation: [you listen and obey what Yahweh your God says]

3.q: בָּר֥וּךְ אַתָּ֖ה בָּ⁠עִ֑יר וּ⁠בָר֥וּךְ אַתָּ֖ה בַּ⁠שָּׂדֶֽה
3.note: Moses is referring to all places where the Israelites will live and work by naming two major components, **the city** and **the field**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [Blessed you will be everywhere you go]

The expression **Blessed you will be** contains a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is God. The same form also occurs in verses 4–6. Alternate translation: [God will bless you in the city and] or [You will receive God’s blessing both in the city and]

4.q: פְּרִֽי־בִטְנְ⁠ךָ֛ וּ⁠פְרִ֥י אַדְמָתְ⁠ךָ֖ וּ⁠פְרִ֣י בְהֶמְתֶּ֑⁠ךָ שְׁגַ֥ר אֲלָפֶ֖י⁠ךָ וְ⁠עַשְׁתְּר֥וֹת צֹאנֶֽ⁠ךָ
4.note: Moses uses a repetitive series of clauses **the fruit of your womb and the fruit of your land and the fruit of your cattle, the increase of your cattle and the young of your flock** to communicate that what he is saying should be understood as comprehensive and overwhelming. Use a form in your language that someone would use to describe a situation that is comprehensive and overwhelming.

Here Moses is speaking as if children, crops, and livestock were **fruit**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [your children and your crops and your livestock]

The terms **increase** and **young** mean similar things. Moses is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [the abundant offspring of your livestock]

5.note: A **basket** is a kind of woven container used for holding food or other items, and a **kneading trough** is a kind of container used for mixing and kneading bread dough. If your readers would not be familiar with what these items are, you could use the names of similar things that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [your food containers and your bread-making bowls] or [the containers you use for food and bread]

Here, **your basket and your kneading trough** represents all of your food and provisions. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [all your food supplies]

6.note: Moses is referring to all of a person’s activities by naming two extremes, **coming in** and **going out**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [everywhere you may go]

7.q: יִתֵּ֨ן יְהוָ֤ה אֶת־אֹיְבֶ֨י⁠ךָ֙ הַ⁠קָּמִ֣ים עָלֶ֔י⁠ךָ נִגָּפִ֖ים לְ⁠פָנֶ֑י⁠ךָ
7.note: The expression **be struck down** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is God. Alternate translation: [Yahweh will strike down to your faces your enemies who rise up against you]
Here, **be struck down** means to be defeated in battle. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [be defeated] or [be conquered]

Here, **to your faces** represents being in your presence or in front of you. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [before you … before you]

Moses says **seven ways** as an extreme statement for emphasis. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a different way to express the emphasis. Alternate translation: [but will flee to your faces in many different directions] or [but will flee to your faces in complete panic]

8.note: Here Moses is speaking of **the blessing** as if it were a living thing that could receive and obey a command. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Yahweh will cause you to be blessed] or [Yahweh will bring blessing to you]

Moses is using **the sending out of your hand** as a common expression of his culture to mean “all of your work and undertakings.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [your endeavors] or [that you do]

9.q: יְקִֽימְ⁠ךָ֨ יְהוָ֥ה ל⁠וֹ֙ לְ⁠עַ֣ם קָד֔וֹשׁ כַּ⁠אֲשֶׁ֖ר נִֽשְׁבַּֽע־לָ֑⁠ךְ כִּ֣י תִשְׁמֹ֗ר אֶת־מִצְוֺת֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔י⁠ךָ וְ⁠הָלַכְתָּ֖ בִּ⁠דְרָכָֽי⁠ו
9.note: Moses is presenting a possible condition, that Yahweh will only establish the Israelites as his sanctified people if they obey Yahweh’s commandments. Use a natural form in your language for introducing a condition that could happen. It may be helpful to reorder this sentence so that the conditional statement is first. Alternate translation: [If you keep the commandments of Yahweh your God and walk in his ways, then Yahweh will establish you as his sanctified people, as he has sworn to you]

Moses is speaking of the **commandments** of Yahweh as if they were **ways** or paths that the person should **walk** on. He means that obeying those commandments is like walking on that path. See how you translated the similar expression in 5:33. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and obey them]

10.note: Moses is using **the name of Yahweh is called upon you** as a common expression of his culture to mean “you belong to Yahweh and are identified as his people.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [you are Yahweh’s people] or [you are identified as belonging to Yahweh]

The expression **is called** is a passive verbal form. If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Yahweh has called you by his name]

11.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **prosperity**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [And Yahweh will make you very prosperous] or [And Yahweh will cause you to have many good things]

11.q: בִּ⁠פְרִ֧י בִטְנְ⁠ךָ֛ וּ⁠בִ⁠פְרִ֥י בְהַמְתְּ⁠ךָ֖ וּ⁠בִ⁠פְרִ֣י אַדְמָתֶ֑⁠ךָ
11.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 28:4.

Here, **your fathers** represents your ancestors. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. See how you translated the phrase “your fathers” in 1:8.

12.q: יִפְתַּ֣ח יְהוָ֣ה ׀ לְ֠⁠ךָ אֶת־אוֹצָר֨⁠וֹ הַ⁠טּ֜וֹב אֶת־הַ⁠שָּׁמַ֗יִם
12.note: Here Moses is speaking of **the heavens** as if they were a physical place where he stored **his treasure** that Yahweh will open to provide rain. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Yahweh will provide abundant rain from the heavens] or [Yahweh will give you the sky’s good gift of rain]

Moses is using one part of a person, his **hand**, to mean all of him in the act of him in the act of working. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression from your culture or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [of your own work]

13.q: וּ⁠נְתָֽנְ⁠ךָ֨ יְהוָ֤ה לְ⁠רֹאשׁ֙ וְ⁠לֹ֣א לְ⁠זָנָ֔ב וְ⁠הָיִ֨יתָ֙ רַ֣ק לְ⁠מַ֔עְלָ⁠ה וְ⁠לֹ֥א תִהְיֶ֖ה לְ⁠מָ֑טָּה כִּֽי־תִשְׁמַ֞ע אֶל־מִצְוֺ֣ת ׀ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֗י⁠ךָ אֲשֶׁ֨ר אָנֹכִ֧י מְצַוְּ⁠ךָ֛ הַ⁠יּ֖וֹם לִ⁠שְׁמֹ֥ר וְ⁠לַ⁠עֲשֽׂוֹת
13.note: Moses is presenting a possible condition beginning with the phrase, that Yahweh will only do the things described in this verse if the Israelites obey Yahweh’s commandments. Use a natural form in your language for introducing a condition that could happen. It may be helpful to reorder this sentence so that the conditional statement is first. Alternate translation: [If you listen to the commandments of Yahweh your God that I am commanding you today, to keep and do, then Yahweh will set you as head, and not as tail; and you will be only above, and you will not be beneath]

13.q: וּ⁠נְתָֽנְ⁠ךָ֨ יְהוָ֤ה לְ⁠רֹאשׁ֙ וְ⁠לֹ֣א לְ⁠זָנָ֔ב וְ⁠הָיִ֨יתָ֙ רַ֣ק לְ⁠מַ֔עְלָ⁠ה וְ⁠לֹ֥א תִהְיֶ֖ה לְ⁠מָ֑טָּה
13.note: These two phrases **Yahweh will set you as head, and not as tail** and **you will be only above, and you will not be beneath** mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [and you will be in a position of honor and not of shame]

Here Moses is comparing Israel’s status among nations to the **head** and **tail** of an animal. He means that the Israelites will be leaders among the nations, not followers. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And Yahweh will make you the leader of nations, and not the follower]

13.q: וְ⁠הָיִ֨יתָ֙ רַ֣ק לְ⁠מַ֔עְלָ⁠ה וְ⁠לֹ֥א תִהְיֶ֖ה לְ⁠מָ֑טָּה
13.note: Here Moses is speaking of Israel’s status among nations as if it were **above** and not **beneath** in physical position. He means that the Israelites will be in a position of authority, not subservience. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and you will be in authority and not subservient]

Moses is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [to keep them and do them]

The terms **keep** and **do** mean similar things. Moses is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [to carefully obey them]

14.q: וְ⁠לֹ֣א תָס֗וּר מִ⁠כָּל־הַ⁠דְּבָרִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר אָנֹכִ֜י מְצַוֶּ֥ה אֶתְ⁠כֶ֛ם הַ⁠יּ֖וֹם יָמִ֣ין וּ⁠שְׂמֹ֑אול
14.note: Moses is speaking as if the Israelites had literally been walking behind God but then could **turn away** to walk in a different direction from him. He means that they should not stop living in the manner in which God wants people to live. See how you translated the similar expression, “Do not turn aside, right or left” in 5:32. Alternate translation: [and you do not disobey Yahweh’s commands that I am giving you today]

Moses is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context of the previous verse if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and if you do not turn away]
The word **you** is plural here, so use the plural form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

Moses is referring to all possible directions of turning away by naming two extremes, **right** and **left**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in any direction] or [at all]

Here Moses is speaking of choosing to worship other gods as if it were literally **going after** them. He is using the image of following someone to mean being devoted to them. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [choosing other gods to serve them]

15.note: Here the phrase **And it will happen, if** introduces a shift from the previous blessings to the curses that will follow disobedience. If the connection between this statement and the previous one is not clear, you may want to use a different connecting word to show how this statement relates to what comes before it. Alternate translation: [However, if]

Here Moses is speaking of **curses** as if they were living beings that could **come upon you and reach you** like hostile pursuers who could chase and capture a person. See how you translated the same phrase “will come upon you and reach you” in relation to blessings in verse 2. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [then all these curses will certainly affect you] or [then you will experience all these curses]

16.note: The expression **Cursed you will be** contains a passive verbal form that occurs here and in verses 17–19. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is Yahweh. Alternate translation: [Yahweh will curse you] or [You will experience Yahweh’s curse]
See how you translated these same phrases in verse 3.

17.note: See how you translated this in verse 5. Alternate translation: [all your food supplies]

18.q: פְּרִֽי־בִטְנְ⁠ךָ֖ וּ⁠פְרִ֣י אַדְמָתֶ֑⁠ךָ שְׁגַ֥ר אֲלָפֶ֖י⁠ךָ וְ⁠עַשְׁתְּר֥וֹת צֹאנֶֽ⁠ךָ
18.note: See how you translated this in verse 4.

19.note: See how you translated this in verse 6

20.q: יְשַׁלַּ֣ח יְהוָ֣ה ׀ בְּ֠⁠ךָ אֶת־הַ⁠מְּאֵרָ֤ה אֶת־הַ⁠מְּהוּמָה֙ וְ⁠אֶת־הַ⁠מִּגְעֶ֔רֶת בְּ⁠כָל־מִשְׁלַ֥ח יָדְ⁠ךָ֖ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תַּעֲשֶׂ֑ה
20.note: If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **curses**, **confusion**, and **rebukes**, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [Yahweh will curse you, confuse you, and rebuke you in everything you do]

The terms **curses**, **confusion**, and **rebukes** mean similar things. Moses is using the three terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [severe judgment] or [complete disaster]
See how you translated “the sending out of your hand” in verse 8. Alternate translation: [your endeavors] or [that you do]

The terms **are destroyed** and **perish** mean similar things. Moses is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [until you are quickly and completely destroyed]

The expression **are destroyed** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is Yahweh. Alternate translation: [until Yahweh destroys you]

Moses is using **from the faces** as a common expression of his culture to mean “because of.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [because of your wicked deeds]
The pronoun **me** refers to Yahweh. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [you will have forsaken Yahweh]

21.note: Here Moses is speaking of **the plague** as if it were a living thing that could **cling to** a person. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [will make the plague remain with you] or [will make the plague stay upon you]

Moses is referring to complete destruction in a polite way by using the phrase **has finished you**. Depending on what is helpful in your language, you could use a polite way of referring to this in your language, or you could state this plainly. Alternate translation: [until he has completely destroyed you]

22.note: Moses is speaking as if Yahweh will actually **strike** or hit the Israelites with these plagues. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [will cause you to suffer]

Moses uses a repetitive series of clauses, **with emaciation and with fever and with inflammation and with fiery heat and with a sword and with scorching winds and with mildew** to communicate that what he is saying should be understood as comprehensive and overwhelming. Use a form in your language that someone would use to describe a situation that is comprehensive and overwhelming.

The terms **emaciation**, **fever**, **inflammation**, and **mildew** refer to various diseases and afflictions. The term **emaciation** describes a wasting disease that causes the body to become extremely thin. The term **fever** describes a condition that causes the body temperature to rise. The term **inflammation** describes a condition that causes parts of the body to become swollen and painful. Here the term **mildew** is describing a fungal disease that can affect crops. If your readers would not be familiar with these specific conditions, you could use more general terms. Alternate translation: [with wasting diseases and with high fever and with painful swelling … and with crop disease]

Here Yahweh is speaking as if he would physically strike the people **with a sword**. He means that he will cause people to die violently in war. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and with violent death in war]

Here Moses is speaking of all these terrible things as if they were living things that could **pursue** people. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [These will continue to affect you until you perish]

23.q: וְ⁠הָי֥וּ שָׁמֶ֛י⁠ךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר עַל־רֹאשְׁ⁠ךָ֖ נְחֹ֑שֶׁת וְ⁠הָ⁠אָ֥רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־תַּחְתֶּ֖י⁠ךָ בַּרְזֶֽל
23.note: Here Moses is speaking of the **skies** as if they were **bronze** and of the **earth** as if it were **iron**. He means that the sky will become hard like bronze and will not give rain, and the ground will become hard like iron and will not produce crops. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the sky above you will give no rain and the ground beneath you will be too hard to plow]

24.note: Here Yahweh is speaking as if **the rain of your land** were **powder and dust**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [no rain to fall on your land, only powder and dust]

The expression **are destroyed** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is Yahweh. Alternate translation: [until Yahweh destroys you]

25.q: יִתֶּנְ⁠ךָ֨ יְהוָ֥ה ׀ נִגָּף֮ לִ⁠פְנֵ֣י אֹיְבֶי⁠ךָ֒ בְּ⁠דֶ֤רֶךְ אֶחָד֙ תֵּצֵ֣א אֵלָ֔י⁠ו וּ⁠בְ⁠שִׁבְעָ֥ה דְרָכִ֖ים תָּנ֣וּס לְ⁠פָנָ֑י⁠ו
25.note: See how you translated the similar sentence in verse 7.

26.note: In this verse, the word **corpse** is singular in form, but it refers to all the Israelites as a group. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use the plural form of “corpse” as modeled in the UST.

By **there will be none to startle them**, Moses means that no one will be alive to drive away the scavenging birds and wild animals from the corpses. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and no one will be left alive to chase them away] or [and no one will remain to frighten them off]

27.note: In the phrase **the boils of Egypt**, Moses is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [with boils like those that afflicted Egypt] or [with the same boils that struck Egypt]

The terms **boils**, **ulcers**, **rash**, and **itch** refer to various kinds of skin diseases. If your readers would not be familiar with what these conditions are, you could use more general terms or explain them in a footnote. Alternate translation: [with painful skin diseases and sores that cause itching]

The expression **to be healed** contains a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [from which you cannot recover] or [which no one can heal]

28.note: Here, **heart** represents the mind or the ability to think clearly. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and with confusion of mind]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **confusion**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and with confused hearts] or [and will confuse your thinking]

29.note: Here Moses is making a comparison. The point of this comparison is that just as **the blind grope in the darkness** and cannot find their way, so the people **will be groping about at noon** and will not be able to find their way or succeed. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [as helplessly as blind people grope in the darkness]

Here Moses is speaking of how a person lives as if that were **ways** or paths that the person was walking along. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [in what you do] or [in your endeavors]

The expression **you shall again be oppressed and robbed** uses passive verbal forms. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [And Yahweh will again allow your enemies to oppress and rob you]
See how you translated the expression “all of the days” in 4:40. Alternate translation: [forever]

31.note: The expression **will be slain** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Someone will slaughter your ox before your eyes]
See how you translated the phrase “before your eyes” in 1:30. Alternate translation: [in your sight]

The expression **will be robbed** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Enemies will steal your donkey] or [People will take your donkey away]

Here, **to your face** represents what is in front of a person. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [from right in front of you] or [while you watch helplessly]

The expression **will be given** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is Yahweh. Alternate translation: [Yahweh will give your sheep to your enemies] or [Your enemies will take your sheep]

32.note: The expression **will be given** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is Yahweh. Alternate translation: [Yahweh will give your sons and your daughters to other peoples] or [Other peoples will take your sons and your daughters away]

Here Moses is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and your eyes will look on your sons and daughters and will long for them]

Here Moses is using one part of a person, **your eyes**, to mean all of you in the act of watching and longing. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and you will watch and will long for them]

33.note: Here, **a nation** represents the people of that nation. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [The people of a nation]

Here, **the fruit of your land and all your labor** represents the crops and goods that result from working the land. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the crops you have produced and everything you have worked to make]

The terms **oppressed** and **crushed** mean similar things. Moses is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [and you will only be mistreated] or [and you will only suffer harm]

Moses is using **all the days** as a common expression of his culture to mean “continually” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have this meaning or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [continually] or [always]

34.note: It might seem that the expression **from the view of your eyes that you will see** contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you could shorten it. Alternate translation: [from all that you will see]

35.note: See how you translated this in verse 22.

Moses is referring to all of the body by naming two extremes, **the bottom of your foot** and **the top of your head**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [all over your body]

36.note: The pronoun **yourself** indicates that the object of the verb is the same as the subject of the verb. Use a way that is natural in your language to indicate that the same person fills two roles in the sentence. Alternate translation: [whom you will choose as your king,]

Moses is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [neither you nor your fathers have known that nation]
Moses is using the term **fathers** to mean “ancestors.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [nor any of your ancestors]

Moses is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [that are made of wood and stone]

37.note: This is poetic language. Here Moses lists three terms that describe the shameful condition Israel will become among the nations. If your language has a way to indicate poetry, you could use it here. Alternate translation: [an object of terror, stories, and scorn]

If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **horror**, **proverb**, and **taunt**, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [something that horrifies people, something that people make proverbs about, and something that people mock]

It might seem that the expression **where Yahweh will drive you there** contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you could shorten it. Alternate translation: [where Yahweh will drive you]

40.q: וְ⁠שֶׁ֨מֶן֙ לֹ֣א תָס֔וּךְ כִּ֥י יִשַּׁ֖ל זֵיתֶֽ⁠ךָ
40.note: The implication is that the **olives** will **become detached**, or fall, from the trees before they are ripe enough to produce **oil**. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [but you will not be able to make oil to grease yourself with, for your olives will fall] or [but you will not grease yourself with oil from your olives, for they will fall]

The expression **will become detached** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is Yahweh. Alternate translation: [Yahweh will cause your olives to fall off]

42.note: Here, **take possession** represents consuming or destroying. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the crickets will devour them]

Moses is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [the crickets will take possession of them]

The term **crickets** refers to a type of small jumping insect, similar to a grasshopper or locust. If your readers would not be familiar with what crickets are, you could use the name of a similar insect that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [insects] or [destructive insects]

43.note: Moses is not referring to a specific **foreigner**. He means foreigners in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Any foreigner who lives among you]

43.q: יַעֲלֶ֥ה עָלֶ֖י⁠ךָ מַ֣עְלָ⁠ה מָּ֑עְלָ⁠ה וְ⁠אַתָּ֥ה תֵרֵ֖ד מַ֥טָּה מָּֽטָּה
43.note: Here Moses is speaking of social status as if it were physical position, with **rise up above you higher and higher** meaning that foreigners will gain increasing social status, wealth, and power, and **descend lower and lower** meaning that the Israelites will lose social status, wealth, and power. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [will become more and more influential than you, while you become less and less influential]

44.q: ה֚וּא יִהְיֶ֣ה לְ⁠רֹ֔אשׁ וְ⁠אַתָּ֖ה תִּֽהְיֶ֥ה לְ⁠זָנָֽב
44.note: Here Moses is speaking of the foreigner’s and the Israelite’s status as if they were the **head** and **tail** of an animal. This means foreigners will have more power and authority than the Israelites. See how you translated the similar phrase, “as head, and not as tail,” in verse 13.

45.q: וּ⁠בָ֨אוּ עָלֶ֜י⁠ךָ כָּל־הַ⁠קְּלָל֣וֹת הָ⁠אֵ֗לֶּה וּ⁠רְדָפ֨וּ⁠ךָ֙ וְ⁠הִשִּׂיג֔וּ⁠ךָ
45.note: Moses is speaking of **all these curses** as if they were living things that could **come upon you and pursue you and reach you** like hostile pursuers who could chase and capture a person. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And all these curses will happen to you and affect you continually and completely overwhelm you]

The terms **commandments** and **statutes** mean similar things. Moses is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. See how you translated the similar expression “his statutes and his commandments” in 4:40. Alternate translation: [his commandments] or [his statutes]

46.note: The terms **signs** and **wonders** mean similar things. Moses is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [as amazing displays] or [as extraordinary demonstrations]

Here Moses is speaking as if the Israelites’ offspring were **seed**. See the Introduction to Deuteronomy for a discussion of this use of the term “seed.” Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and on your descendants] or [and on your offspring]

47.note: If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **joyfulness** and **gladness**, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [joyfully and gladly because you had an abundance of everything]

The terms **joyfulness** and **gladness of heart** mean similar things. Moses is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [with great joy] or [with deep happiness]

Here, **heart** represents a person’s inner being and emotions. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and with gladness in your inner being] or [and with an attitude of gladness]

48.note: Here Moses is speaking as if the enemy’s oppression were **a yoke of iron** placed on the Israelites’ necks. This image emphasizes that the oppression will be harsh, inescapable, and degrading, like the heavy iron yoke that would be put on a work animal. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And he will make you slaves under harsh and inescapable oppression]

49.note: Here Moses is using speaking as if Yahweh were going to **lift up a nation** physically into a higher place than Israel. He means that Yahweh will bring them to a position of power over Israel. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Yahweh will bring a nation against you] or [Yahweh will raise up a nation against you]

Moses says **from the ends of the earth** as an extreme statement for emphasis. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a different way to express the emphasis. Alternate translation: [from a very distant land]

The point of this comparison is that just as **an eagle flies** swiftly and attacks suddenly, so this nation will attack swiftly and suddenly. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [attacking swiftly like an eagle swooping down on its prey]

50.note: Moses is using **fierce of face** as a common expression of his culture to mean “cruel and intimidating in appearance.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [that is ruthless] or [that is cruel and intimidating]

Moses is using **lift up a face** as a common expression of his culture to mean “be partial to someone.” When he uses “does not lift up a face for the elder,” he means “does not show respect for” or “does not show favor to.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [shows no respect for the elder] or [treats the elder without honor]

51.note: Both occurrences of the pronoun **it** refer to the “nation” mentioned in the previous verse. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers.
See how you translated the similar expression “the fruit of your land and the fruit of your cattle” in verse 4.

The expression **are destroyed** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [until the nation destroys you] or [until you perish]

52.note: Both occurrences of the pronoun **it** refer to the “nation” mentioned in the verse 50. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers.

Moses is using one part of a city or town, the **gates**, to mean walled cities or towns in general. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [within all your cities] or [within all your towns]

53.note: Moses is using **fruit of your womb** as a common expression of his culture to mean “your children.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [your own children]

54.note: The terms **tender** and **very delicate** mean similar things. Moses is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [The most gentle man among you]

Moses is not referring to a specific **tender man**. He means any man who has lived a pampered life in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Any pampered man] or [Even a man who is tender]

Moses is using **his eye will do wrong against** as a common expression of his culture to mean “he will look with malice and act selfishly toward.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [he will be selfish toward his brother] or [he will act with malice toward his brother]

Moses is using **the wife of his bosom** as a common expression of his culture to mean “his beloved wife” or “his dear wife.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and against his own dear wife]

It might seem that the expression **remainder of his children who remain** contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you could shorten. Alternate translation: [and against the remainder of his children]

55.note: Moses is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [since nothing remains for himself to eat]

The word **himself** indicates that the object of the verb is the same as the subject of the verb. Use a way that is natural in your language to indicate that the same person fills two roles in the sentence. Alternate translation: [for him]
See how you translated the same expression in verse 52.

56.note: Moses is not referring to a specific **delicate woman**. He means delicate women in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and any delicate woman]

Moses says **would not attempt to set the bottom of her foot on the ground** as an extreme statement for emphasis. It could mean that the woman has always had servants to carry her places or that she’s always had shoes to protect her feet from the cold and dirt of the ground. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a different way to express the emphasis. Alternate translation: [who has always been carried everywhere] or [who has always had clean, warm feet]
See how you translated the similar expression “his eye will do wrong against his brother and against the wife of his bosom” in verse 54.

57.note: Moses is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [for lack of anything else to eat]

57.q: בְּ⁠מָצוֹר֙ וּ⁠בְ⁠מָצ֔וֹק אֲשֶׁ֨ר יָצִ֥יק לְ⁠ךָ֛ אֹיִבְ⁠ךָ֖ בִּ⁠שְׁעָרֶֽי⁠ךָ
57.note: Here Moses is speaking of **the distress** as if it were something physical that an enemy could **set upon** people. He means that the enemy will cause the people to experience distress. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [in the siege and in the distress that your enemy will cause you to experience within your gates]
See how you translated the phrase “within all your gates” in verse 52.

58.q: אִם־לֹ֨א תִשְׁמֹ֜ר לַ⁠עֲשׂ֗וֹת אֶת־כָּל־דִּבְרֵי֙ הַ⁠תּוֹרָ֣ה הַ⁠זֹּ֔את
58.note: Here, **If you do not keep doing all the words of this law** introduces the first part of a possible condition. Yahweh will only do the things in verse 59 if this condition happens. Use a natural form in your language for introducing a condition that could happen. Alternate translation: [Suppose you do not keep doing all the words of this law]

The expression **are written** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is Yahweh. Alternate translation: [that Yahweh has given me to write]

58.q: אֶת־הַ⁠שֵּׁ֞ם הַ⁠נִּכְבָּ֤ד וְ⁠הַ⁠נּוֹרָא֙ הַ⁠זֶּ֔ה אֵ֖ת יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶֽי⁠ךָ
58.note: Here, **name** represents Yahweh himself, including his character, power, and reputation. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Yahweh your God himself, who is glorious and to be revered]

If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **glorious** and **feared**, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [this name that brings glory and terror] or [this name that people glorify and revere]

59.note: See how you translated the expression “your seed” in verse 46. Alternate translation: [your offspring]

Moses is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and they will be great and enduring sicknesses]

60.note: Moses is using **of which you were afraid of their faces** as a common expression of his culture to mean “which you feared” or “which terrified you.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [which you feared]

61.note: Moses is saying **every sickness and every plague that is not written** as a generalization for emphasis. If it would be clearer in your language, you could express the emphasis in a different way. Alternate translation: [many other sicknesses and plagues that are not written]

61.q: אֲשֶׁר֙ לֹ֣א כָת֔וּב בְּ⁠סֵ֖פֶר הַ⁠תּוֹרָ֣ה הַ⁠זֹּ֑את
61.note: The expression **is not written** contains a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [that I have not written in the scroll of this law] or [that this law does not record]

The expression **are destroyed** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [until they destroy you]

62.note: The words translated **you shall remain** and **you were** are plural here because Moses is addressing the Israelites as a group, but **you did not listen** is singular because it refers to each individual Israelite. So use the plural form for the first two phrases and the singular form for the last phrase in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

Here Moses is making a comparison between the number of Israelites and **the stars of the heavens**. The point of this comparison is that just as **the stars of the heavens** are countless, so were the Israelites numerous in the past. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [you were as countless as the stars of the heavens] or [you were very numerous]

63.note: The word **you** is plural throughout most of this verse because Moses is addressing the Israelites as a group. However, in the final clause the **you** is singular, referring to the nation of Israel as a single entity. Use the appropriate form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

63.q: כַּ⁠אֲשֶׁר־שָׂ֨שׂ יְהוָ֜ה עֲלֵי⁠כֶ֗ם לְ⁠הֵיטִ֣יב אֶתְ⁠כֶם֮ וּ⁠לְ⁠הַרְבּ֣וֹת אֶתְ⁠כֶם֒ כֵּ֣ן יָשִׂ֤ישׂ יְהוָה֙ עֲלֵי⁠כֶ֔ם לְ⁠הַאֲבִ֥יד אֶתְ⁠כֶ֖ם וּ⁠לְ⁠הַשְׁמִ֣יד אֶתְ⁠כֶ֑ם
63.note: Moses uses the word **so** here to indicate a contrast between Yahweh’s past joy in blessing Israel and his future joy in punishing them. This creates a shocking reversal of expectations—the same divine joy that once brought blessing will bring destruction. In your translation, indicate this contrast in a way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [just as Yahweh rejoiced over you in doing you good and in multiplying you, in the same way Yahweh will rejoice over you in causing you to perish and in destroying you]

Here Moses is speaking as if the Israelites were plants that would be **torn away** from the soil. He means that they will be forcibly removed from the land. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And you will be forcibly removed from the land] or [And you will be driven out of the land]

The expression **you will be torn away from the land** contains a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is Yahweh. Alternate translation: [And Yahweh will tear you away from the land]

64.note: Moses is referring to all of the earth by naming two extremes, **one end of the earth** and **the other end of the earth**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [everywhere on earth] or [to the farthest places on earth]

65.note: Moses is using one part of a person, the **sole of your foot**, to mean all of him in the act of finding rest. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [there will be no rest for you]

65.q: לֵ֣ב רַגָּ֔ז וְ⁠כִלְי֥וֹן עֵינַ֖יִם וְ⁠דַֽאֲב֥וֹן נָֽפֶשׁ
65.note: Here, **a trembling heart**, **failing eyes**, and **a mourning spirit** represent fearfulness, hopelessness, and deep sadness. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use equivalent expressions or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [fearfulness, hopelessness, and despair] or [constant fear, lost hope, and deep sadness]

66.note: Here Moses is speaking as if the people’s lives could physically **hang** precariously, as if suspended by a thread. He means that their lives will constantly be at risk and they will live in uncertainty about their survival. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [your life will constantly be at risk] or [you will live in constant danger]

Moses is referring to all times by naming two extremes, **night** and **day**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [all the time] or [constantly]

67.q: בַּ⁠בֹּ֤קֶר תֹּאמַר֙ מִֽי־יִתֵּ֣ן עֶ֔רֶב וּ⁠בָ⁠עֶ֥רֶב תֹּאמַ֖ר מִֽי־יִתֵּ֣ן בֹּ֑קֶר
67.note: Moses is using the question form to express the people’s despair and longing for relief from their suffering. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate these questions as statements or as exclamations. Alternate translation: [In the morning you will say, ‘I wish it were evening!’ and in the evening you will say, ‘I wish it were morning!’]

Moses is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [because of the great fear you feel]

It might seem that the expression **from the view of your eyes that you will see** contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you could shorten it. Alternate translation: [all that you will see]

68.note: Here the pronoun **I** refers to Yahweh. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Yahweh had said] or [he had said]

68.q: בַּ⁠דֶּ֨רֶךְ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָמַ֣רְתִּֽי לְ⁠ךָ֔ לֹא־תֹסִ֥יף ע֖וֹד לִ⁠רְאֹתָ֑⁠הּ
68.note: Here, **see** represents experiencing. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [by the route which he had said to you, ‘You will not go there again.’]

68.q: וְ⁠הִתְמַכַּרְתֶּ֨ם שָׁ֧ם לְ⁠אֹיְבֶ֛י⁠ךָ לַ⁠עֲבָדִ֥ים וְ⁠לִ⁠שְׁפָח֖וֹת וְ⁠אֵ֥ין קֹנֶֽה
68.note: Moses says **but there will be no buyers** as an overstatement for emphasis. This is the climax of the judgment prophecies, expressing poetic irony: the people will be so desperate that they will try to sell themselves back into slavery, but they will be so numerous and so worthless as slaves that no one will buy them. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a different way to express the emphasis. Alternate translation: [If you were to try to sell yourselves to your enemies as slaves, your people will be so numerous and so worthless that you would find no one willing to buy you]
The word **you** is plural here, so use the plural form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.
